title: Study verbs and their cases
summary: Use the lemma given. Вчити/вивчати a subject takes the accusative; навчати someone takes the accusative and the subject taught takes the genitive. Керувати/завідувати take the instrumental; директор/завідувач take the genitive. A lemma cue fixes the word even where meanings overlap.

study-math.note: Accusative: вчу takes the accusative — what is studied.

learn-topic.sentenceGloss: We are studying a new topic.

teach-math.note: Genitive: навчати takes the genitive — what is taught.

teach-student.sentenceGloss: The lecturer teaches the new student.
teach-student.note: Accusative: навчати takes the accusative — the person taught.

teach-physics.note: Genitive: навчати takes the genitive — what is taught.

head-college.sentenceGloss: He is in charge of the technical college.

director-school.sentenceGloss: This is the school headteacher's office.
director-school.note: Genitive: the noun in the second case after директора.

head-department.sentenceGloss: The head of department came to the meeting.
head-department.note: Genitive: the noun in the second case after завідувач.

knowledge-dat.sentenceGloss: Thanks to his broad knowledge he explained the difficult topic.

paint-inst.sentenceGloss: The child paints with bright paints.
paint-inst.note: Instrumental: the tool or material takes the instrumental.

hues-inst.note: Instrumental: the instrument of the verb takes the instrumental.

scissors-gen.sentenceGloss: There are no scissors in the pencil case.
scissors-gen.note: Genitive plural: ножиці in the second case plural after немає.

notebook-loc.sentenceGloss: Oleh wrote the rule in his exercise book.
notebook-loc.note: Locative singular: зошит in the second case singular.

ruler-inst.sentenceGloss: It is convenient to draw a straight line with a ruler.
ruler-inst.note: Instrumental: the instrument of the verb takes the instrumental.
